newsitem.title: ITALY: Feed earthlings, not Martians, summit told.
newsitem.headline: Feed earthlings, not Martians, summit told.

text.p: The tiny coral Pacific island of Niue injected an extra-terrestrial note to a U.N. food summit on Saturday, saying feeding the Earth's hungry was a better way to spend money than unlocking the secrets of Mars.

"I would like to reassure those countries who are spending billions of dollars in trying to find out whether there is life on the red planet Mars that there is life on Earth," said Frank Lui, prime minister of Niue.
"Earthlings need nourishment much more than any Martians," he said.

Seizing the opportunity to draw media attention to the island of 2,500 people, on a day dominated by the arrival of Cuban leader Fidel Castro, Lui broke with the general gloom of the summit to tell how Nieu enjoyed "plentiful food all year round".
The islanders had rich tropical soil and access to marine life in the "clean clear waters of the Pacific", he said.
But he said the remote island had not forgotten the plight of the hungry despite having access to "some of Nature's abundant bounties".
"As small and isloated as we are, we are still very much part of this planet," he declared.

Niue is about 480 km (300 miles) east of Tonga and 930 km (580 miles) west of the southern Cook Islands. The country enjoys self-government in free association with New Zealand, which remains in control of defence and external affairs.
There are 1,271 men on the island and 1,260 women.
